gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Garmin vívoactive 5 sells new for $169.99 today (HRM USA, crossed out from $269.99). That is $100 below the $269.99 ChatGPT showed and $130 below the Amazfit Balance 2 and vívoactive 6, which are both $299.99.
standout_why: Compared against cubicalgolfer.com/best-golf-gps-watch-under-300, clubandcarry.com/golf-tech/best-value-watches, outdoorgearlab.com best-gps-watch (cited), garmin.com/en-US/blog whats-the-best-garmin-golf-watch-for-me and the Garmin S44/S50 press release (cited). OutdoorGearLab lists the vívoactive 6 at $300 and doesn't mention the vívoactive 5 or golf. The Garmin blog leaves out the vívoactive line and gives no prices. Cubicalgolfer and Club & Carry rank only golf-first watches (S12, S42, S44, Shot Scope V5, Bushnell Ion Elite) and never mention heart rate or sleep. None of them states the $169.99 vívoactive 5 price. It isn't scored 3 because the price comes from a Garmin dealer, not garmin.com, which did not render a price for me.
decides: This confirms the vívoactive 5 as the value pick and widens its lead. For $169.99 it has wrist heart rate and sleep tracking plus a golf menu with hazards, layups, scorecard, PinPointer and last-shot tracking. The S44 at $299.99 has no heart-rate sensor. The vívoactive 6 costs $130 more and adds View Green, Measure Shot and Club Stats. The Balance 2 also costs $130 more, so its 21-day battery and free golf maps have to justify the difference. For the chat that put the Balance 2 first, this price undercuts that ranking.
